  • Genomic DNA extraction (MasterPure Yeast kit)

    By Various authorsVersion 1Updated 2026-10-07

    Purifying genomic DNA from a liquid culture pellet or a single colony.

5 protocols

Phenotyping & imaging

Colony selection and measuring cluster size, cell shape, cell volume and ploidy

  • Colony selection from plates

    By Various authorsVersion 1Updated 2026-10-07

    Recognising true snowflake clones (“volcano” or “donut” colonies) when picking from plates.

  • Measuring cell aspect ratio

    By Various authorsVersion 1Updated 2026-10-07

    Calcofluor White staining and ×40 imaging for Cellpose-based cell shape measurements.

  • Measuring cell volume

    By Various authorsVersion 1Updated 2026-10-07

    Crushing clusters to a single layer, then Calcofluor staining and imaging to estimate cell volume as an ellipsoid.

  • Measuring cluster size

    By Various authorsVersion 1Updated 2026-10-07

    Imaging cluster cross-sectional area after 5 days of settling selection, for size segmentation.

  • Measuring ploidy (propidium iodide staining)

    By Various authorsVersion 1Updated 2026-10-07

    Staining DNA with propidium iodide and imaging to measure ploidy against known diploid and tetraploid controls.

  • CRISPR-Cas9 knock-in at the ChrXIII Int8 locus

    By Various authorsVersion 1Updated 2026-10-07

    Single-locus knock-ins (e.g. GFP labelling) in the Y55 background, with Golden Gate–built Cas9 and donor plasmids (constitutive TEF or inducible promoter).

  • Lithium acetate/PEG transformation of snowflake yeast

    By Various authorsVersion 1Updated 2026-10-07

    The standard LiOAc/PEG transformation adapted for multicellular clusters, for plasmids, PCR products or CRISPR constructs.

The experiment

The Multicellularity Long-Term Evolution Experiment is run by the Ratcliff Lab in the School of Biological Sciences at the Georgia Institute of Technology.

Support

NSF Long-Term Research in Environmental Biology (LTREB), Award 2452109. Earlier and concurrent support from NIH NIGMS, NASA Exobiology, the John Templeton Foundation and the Packard Foundation.
